name: held-out example
wording: An example the architect holds back from the builders when a story's risk warrants, kept with the design apart from the visible examples; the lead gives it to the story's reviewers and to no one else, so passing the visible examples while missing the concept is caught. It is held back by omission alone, never named in a task or mentioned to a builder, since a prohibition would announce it. When one fails, builders learn the concept and the shortfall but not the case, and a case revealed to fix it becomes visible and is replaced by a new held-out one.
reason: Raised by the lead realizing intent-based delegation, 2026-10-15. Who hands held-out examples to reviewers was unstated: the lead dispatches the reviewers, so it hands them on, never naming them in a task.
